narrative: Material PL2__MBB28FF8 shows erratic daily demand averaging 2,242 units (CV=41.9%) with no statistically significant trend over the observation window. Lead times are highly unstable (CV=117%), clustering near zero but with occasional spikes to ~3 days. The current SAP policy carries zero safety stock, creating substantial stockout risk; the recommended (r,Q) continuous-review policy introduces a 3,186-unit safety stock to achieve 95% service level, with replenishments triggered at 6,479 units and capped at 21,638 units per order due to storage constraints.
warnings: Storage capacity constraint binds: unconstrained EOQ (83,447) far exceeds available storage; order quantity capped at 21,638 units.
SAP safety lead time (4.0 days) significantly exceeds data-supported value (1.42 days) — recommend reduction.
Lead time CV = 117.1% — highly unstable supply; monitor supplier performance closely.

research_insights.selection_rationale: Erratic demand with unstable lead times makes a fixed-reorder-point continuous-review policy optimal. Periodic review would accumulate unacceptable risk between cycles given the high demand variability and frequent near-zero lead times punctuated by multi-day spikes.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage capacity is fully utilised at the recommended policy (SS+OQ = 24,824 units vs limit 24,824.49). Any upward revision to safety stock or order quantity is infeasible without capacity expansion. At peak demand periods, service level may slightly underperform the 95% target.
research_insights.escalation_flag: None — MOQ (983) + safety_stock (3,186) = 4,169 which is well below max_storage_units (24,824). No MOQ-capacity conflict exists.
